page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.g5 family. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 24 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, supported by 96.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity is provided via an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 are rated in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also demonstrate average performance, though the Passmark memory score itself is weak.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core scaling, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads that can leverage parallel processing. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, Redis database operations, and medium-sized language model inference. Because single-core performance is weak, it is less optimal for single-threaded execution paths. From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable multi-threaded execution, making it a stable option for standard enterprise applications that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with a KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps. Benchmark data shows weak single-core CPU performance and poor single-threaded compression speeds, but multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently reach average tiers. This makes the instance highly capable for parallelized tasks. It is best suited for multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, Redis operations, and moderate LLM text generation, offering a stable, dedicated resource profile for standard enterprise applications.
